liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **When a Man Loves a Woman (Abbreviated)** (1 review): Reviewer hears someone cough up a rough vocal here, guessing it was Bob [3]
- Uploader tentatively identifies this piece as possibly One Way Out [1]

## Setlist highlights

- **When a Man Loves a Woman (Abbreviated)**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [5]
- **Phil Tuning**: back after 1542 archived shows (7909 days); rare: 3 archived performances [5]
- **Schoolgirl (1)**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [5]
- **Schoolgirl (2)**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [5]
- **Jerry�s ABB Idea**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [5]
- **Schoolgirl (3)**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [5]
- **The ABB Idea Considered**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [5]
- **Neighbor Neighbor**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [5]

## The recordings

- **gd1995-03-28.sndchk.fm.GEMS.80018.sbeok.flac16** (recommended): soundboard; 18 songs; 44 min [1]. Said about its sound: The static heard is from attempts to fine-tune Jerry's ear monitor; frequencies shifted nightly and sat very close together; Reviewer finds annoying static throughout, yet considers it interesting to hear the band working through it [1][3]

## Around the show

- Reviewer says the band did not play a concert at the Omni on this date [2]
- Reviewer says no concert occurred this date; it was an off day during a four-night Omni run [4]
- Reviewer identifies the recording as a soundcheck or rehearsal rather than a show [4]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1995-03-28.sndchk.fm.GEMS.80018.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Mike Townshend; source: FM SBD Monitor -> MC -> Cass (Maxell XLII 90) [1]. Also: Recorded in an office inside the Omni, not from the concert hall itself; Reviewer notes the recording was made from an office inside The Omni, and thinks the band was fiddling with sound [1][3]
